goetzmann0381: The Imperial Russian Commission for the Repayment of State Debts issued this perpetual bearer bond in 1839, registering it in the State Debt Book in the name of its Administration. Its face capital is 5,000 rubles, stated expressly in assignats, the paper currency then trading well below silver. The bond pays a perpetual income of six percent a year, 300 rubles, in half-yearly portions of 150 rubles each January and July. It was registered in January of the year of issue.
goetzmann0382: Fifty yen, the eighty-eighth issue of premium savings bonds sold by the Nippon Kangyō Bank, the government-linked Hypothec Bank of Japan, dated November 1938. The bank sold the bond to the public at a discounted price of ten yen; the gap between that price and the redemption value stood in place of interest. An attached prize drawing offered lottery-style bonuses to holders.
goetzmann0383: A wartime patriotic bond of five yen face value, fourth series, dated August 1942. The issuer named at left is the Nippon Kangyō Bank, the semi-official mortgage bank through which the government placed small-denomination war loans rather than the treasury directly. Premium terms printed at right attach a lottery to the instrument: a detachable coupon at the foot entered the bearer in periodic prize drawings. A red seal reads "Greater East Asia War," the official Japanese name for the Pacific conflict.
goetzmann0384: Ten yen, fourth series, dated August 1942. The legend on the right panel states that this wartime patriotic bond funded the imperial treasury under the authority of the Ministry of Finance, while the name and seal at left show that it was placed through the Nippon Kangyō Bank. Repayment carried a premium awarded by periodic lottery drawing, and the detachable coupon below carries the matching number. The central seal names the Greater East Asia War.
goetzmann0385: Part of a 4.5 percent loan of 1912 for the Kahetian Railway Company, raised on a nominal capital of 13,230,000 rubles, or 1,400,000 pounds sterling. Each bearer bond carries a face value of 189 rubles, fixed at 20 pounds sterling, and runs in parallel Russian and English text. It was issued at St. Petersburg in 1912 with the express sanction of the Imperial Russian Government. The loan financed a railway through the Kakheti wine country of eastern Georgia, joining Tiflis, now Tbilisi, to its vineyards.
goetzmann0386: Issued under the Imperial Russian Government's 4 percent State Loan of 1902, this bearer bond of 1,000 Imperial German marks pays 4 percent annual interest. The face equates the marks to 463 rubles 50 kopecks, 590 Dutch guilders, and 49 pounds sterling, and registers the holder in the State Debt Book. The Highest Ukase of March 1, 1902 authorized the loan to cover Russia's losses from the Boxer Rebellion in China, its share of the indemnity imposed on the Chinese government the previous year. The loan's nominal capital reached 181,950,000 rubles, or 393,000,000 marks.
goetzmann0387: The Imperial Ukase of December 15, 1904 authorized this 4.5 percent Russian State Loan of 1905. The bearer bond's face value of 500 Imperial German marks is restated as 231 rubles 50 kopecks, 294 Dutch guilders, and 24 pounds 7 shillings 6 pence sterling, the multiple denominations of a loan placed at once across several European exchanges. The whole issue totaled 231,500,000 rubles. The holder is entered in the State Debt Book.
goetzmann0388: A Dutch chain declaration, or "kettingverklaring," issued at Amsterdam on January 24, 1941, used when foreign securities changed hands. It registers a 100-guilder share in De Woning Maatschappij Batavia, a housing company in the Netherlands East Indies, then a Dutch colony. The form was certified by the Vereeniging voor den Effectenhandel, the association of securities traders, and requested by an Amsterdam member; the alternative Rotterdam and The Hague memberships are struck through. It invokes a decree of September 18, 1940 and article 10 of the 1940 foreign-exchange ordinance imposed under German occupation, and attests that the security was registered and could pass between residents without a separate declaration.
goetzmann0389: This transferable subscription right was issued by the Royal Dutch Petroleum Company at The Hague in February 1937. Against surrender of the warrant, the bearer could buy one new share of 1,000 guilders nominal for 4,500 guilders up to March 31, 1940, or for 5,000 guilders from April 1, 1940 until the right expired on March 31, 1943. The company, chartered in 1890, was by then the Dutch partner in the Royal Dutch/Shell group.
goetzmann0390: Ten thousand kronen at 5.5 percent annual tax-free interest, issued by the Imperial-Royal treasury at Vienna on October 1, 1915. The bond belongs to the Third Austrian War Loan, one of a series floated by Austria-Hungary to fund its part in the war. Coupons fell due each January 1 and July 1, and repayment was promised from 1930. The 10,000-krone denomination was among the largest offered.
goetzmann0391: A bearer share for one hundred francs of the capital of La Pelleterie Russo-Américaine, dated Paris, 31 July 1926. The company was a French joint-stock concern seated at 1 Place des Victoires in Paris, incorporated before the notary Maître Dufour, with a capital of five million francs divided into 4,000 dividend shares and 46,000 capital shares, of which this is one. It traded in furs drawn from Russia and North America. Printed by Imp. Max-Chesnitz of Paris.
goetzmann0392: A share warrant to bearer, given under the common seal of La Platense Flotilla Company, Limited at Glasgow on 20 March 1886, certifying its holder as proprietor of one fully paid share of £10. The company was capitalized at £1,000,000 in 100,000 such shares and was formed to work a steam flotilla on the Río de la Plata and its tributaries. The text runs in parallel English and French, and a three-shilling impressed duty stamp is cancelled by a Scottish revenue postmark of 25 March 1886. Printed by Maclure & MacDonald Ltd of Glasgow.
goetzmann0393: A fragment of ancient papyrus, torn and holed, bearing several lines of cursive script in Greek or Coptic, the everyday administrative hand of Egypt under Ptolemaic, Roman, or Byzantine rule, roughly the third century BCE to the seventh century CE. The content cannot be read with confidence from the fragment. Documents of this form are typically financial or administrative: a tax receipt, a grain account, a loan agreement, or a land lease.
goetzmann0394: An engraved certificate for ten shares of fifty dollars each in the capital stock of the Little Miami Rail Road Company, issued at Cincinnati on June 17, 1862, in the name of James G. King's Sons, the New York banking house acting here as trustees. The company was chartered under the State of Ohio, and the stock is transferable only on its own books upon surrender of the instrument. It was incorporated in 1836 to link Cincinnati with the interior toward Springfield. Engraved by Rawdon, Wright & Hatch of Cincinnati.
goetzmann0395: A bearer treasury bill of 1,000 guilders at 8 percent interest, part of the 8 percent Lung-Tsing-U-Hai Railway Treasury Bill loan of 1923 issued by the Government of the Chinese Republic. The whole issue of 16,667,000 guilders was divided into 16,667 bills of 1,000 guilders each. The railway was planned to run from Gansu in the northwest across Shaanxi and Henan to the Jiangsu coast. The bill was placed on the Netherlands market through the N.V. Nederlandsch Syndicaat voor China, whose name appears at the foot, and its text runs in parallel Dutch and Chinese.
goetzmann0396: A printed and hand-completed instrument, dated at Providence, April 1, 1858, recording the transfer of twelve shares of the capital stock of the Merchants Insurance Company. It was executed "for value received" by the assigning shareholder in favor of James S. Ham and attested by a witness. The left border states the par value at fifty dollars a share, placing the holding's nominal worth at six hundred dollars. The company was one of the marine and fire insurers serving the maritime trade and textile mills of Rhode Island.
goetzmann0397: A certificate for twenty-five shares of capital stock in The Mexican Telephone Company, issued at New York City on February 28, 1905, each share of ten dollars par value. It names Harry E. Jacobs of Cambridge as holder and required countersignature by the Boston Safe Deposit & Trust Company as transfer agent. The company was organized under the laws of the State of New York with an authorized capital of $2,000,000 divided into 200,000 shares. The legend "Issued for Property Purchased" marks these shares as consideration paid in kind rather than cash.
goetzmann0398: A share warrant to bearer certifying that its holder is the registered proprietor of twenty-five fully paid preference shares of £1 each in Minas Geraes Goldfields Limited, numbered 34,983 to 35,007, in a company incorporated under the Companies Acts 1862 to 1900 with a capital of £150,000. It was given under the common seal of the company at London on the first day of July 1912, and bears an impressed stamp duty of seven shillings and sixpence. Its text runs in parallel English and French. The company worked gold-mining ground in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais, spelled "Minas Geraes" in the period. Printed by Imp. F. Fano, 16 Rue du Grand-Prieuré, Paris.
goetzmann0399: A fully paid bearer share of one hundred francs in the Société Anonyme des Mines d'Or de Nam Kok, its issue authorized in the Journal Officiel of 6 November 1929 as recorded by the stamp-duty notice on the certificate. The company was a gold-mining concern domiciled in Paris, capitalized at 30,000,000 francs, its statutes deposited with Maître Ader, notary in Paris. The share entitles the holder to the full sheet of dividend coupons printed below it. Printed by P. Forveille, printer of securities, Paris-Rodez.
goetzmann0400: A bearer bond from the 4 percent loan of 1901 of the Moscow-Kazan Railway Company, issued under the perpetual guarantee of the Imperial Russian Government. Its face value of 2,000 German imperial marks is restated in the principal markets of issue as 925 rubles 80 kopecks, at 1 ruble to 2.16 marks, 1,180 Dutch guilders, and 97 pounds 18 shillings, against a total loan capital of 35,880,000 marks. It was printed at Moscow in 1901 in parallel Russian, German, and Dutch columns, and was placed simultaneously in the German and Netherlands capital markets.
goetzmann0401: A single sheet bearing two engraved stock-transfer assignments of the Morris Canal and Banking Company, executed at its agency at the Phenix Bank in the City of New York and dated June 28 and July 10, 1845. Each is a printed "For Value Received" form by which a holder assigns and transfers shares in the capital stock of the company's "OF 1844" issue, standing in the holder's name on the company's books, to be subscribed before a witness. The company was chartered in New Jersey in 1824 to operate the Morris Canal, joining a public work to banking privileges.
goetzmann0402: A debt certificate for one thousand dollars issued by The New York Central and Hudson River Railroad Company and dated December 1892, bearing interest at four percent a year payable twice yearly. Its terms specify that the principal shall not fall due until the first day of May 1902, and that both principal and interest are payable in gold coin of the United States "of the standard of weight and fineness" then prevailing. The certificate is a form of medium-term borrowing the road used alongside its bonded debt and equity.
goetzmann0403: An engraved $1,000 bond of the New York Central Rail Road Company, dated the first day of August 1858. It certifies that the holder, being a stockholder in one or more of the several railroad companies authorized to be consolidated, is entitled to one thousand dollars, to be paid out of the revenues arising from the road, with interest at six percent a year payable half-yearly on the last day of May and the first day of November against the interest warrants apportioned to it, payable in the City of New York. The certificate is transferable only on the books of the company, upon surrender and written assignment. It is signed by the president and the treasurer and struck with a large red CANCELLED stamp. The company had been formed in 1853 by consolidating the lines linking Albany to Buffalo.
goetzmann0404: A registered first mortgage gold bond of $10,000, signed at New York in November 1904, bearing four percent annual interest and issued by the New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad Company under its Harlem River–Port Chester Branch First Mortgage. Its fifty-year term runs from the first day of November 1904 to maturity on the first day of May 1954, with principal and interest payable in United States gold coin at the company's New York office. The bond is stamped SURRENDERED.
goetzmann0405: A share certificate, or luogo, in the Nuovo Monte Sussidio Vacabile della Città di Firenze, the New Vacatable Subsidy Fund of the City of Florence, dated at Florence on 11 August 1706. Handwritten on a letterpress form, it was issued by the fund's Protectors, Deputies and Administrators under the Grand Duke of Tuscany, and records the holder as creditor for one hundred ducats of Florentine money per luogo, yielding six percent yearly. It rests on the fund's founding provision of 4 July 1692 and a decree of amplification of 8 August 1692. In a monte vacabile the income reverted to the fund on the holder's death, blending a bond with a life annuity.
goetzmann0406: A bearer obligation of the Compañía del Ferro-Carril de Palencia á Ponferrada, dated at Madrid, 15 June 1862, and sanctioned by royal decree of 18 May 1862 under a ninety-nine-year concession. It is one of an issue of 68,420 obligations of 1,900 reales vellón, or 500 francs, each bearing 57 reales, 15 francs, of annual interest payable each 15 June and 15 December, redeemable at par by annual lottery drawings over ninety-two years from 1 July 1867, against a headline total of 65,000,000 reales. Its text runs in parallel Spanish and French. The line crossed the Cantabrian range to link the Castilian grain plains with the coal of El Bierzo.
goetzmann0407: A printed coupon bond for $1,000 of the Norwich & Worcester Rail Road Company, chartered in the State of Connecticut, dated at Hartford with the day and year left blank: this is an unissued remainder. It bears six percent interest payable twice yearly on presentation of the attached coupons, with the principal payable to the Treasurer of the State of Connecticut at the New England Trust Company in Boston. The whole authorized amount of the issue is $500,000. That the bond runs to the State Treasurer marks it as security for Connecticut's aid to the line linking Norwich, on the Thames, with Worcester in Massachusetts.
goetzmann0408: A handwritten libramiento, or treasury payment order, of the Spanish colonial Real Hacienda at Lima, dated July 1816, promising payment one year later of 500 silver pesos. It was drawn against the Empréstito Patriótico, an emergency forced loan levied on the population of Lima to finance the royalist war effort during the South American wars of independence. It carries 5 percent annual interest, the twenty-five pesos named on its face being that five percent of the 500-peso principal. Peru remained under Spanish rule until 1821. A later notation of 1817 records further processing.
goetzmann0409: A bearer bond of the Imperial Russian 5 percent Internal Prize Loan of 1864, with a capital value of 100 rubles yielding 5 rubles a year. Its text is set in parallel Russian and German, showing that the loan was meant to circulate in German financial markets as well as at home. A prize loan married a fixed coupon to periodic lottery draws for large cash prizes.
goetzmann0410: A bearer share of 100 francs, Series A, in the Omnium Français du Film, dated 10 May 1928 and certified before Maître Baudrier, notary in Paris. The company was a Paris joint-stock concern with a capital of three million francs, divided into 30,000 shares of 100 francs each, 26,000 of Series A and 4,000 of Series B, alongside 12,000 founder's shares carrying no nominal value. Printed by Imp. J. Crémieux.
goetzmann0411: A printed and manuscript dividend receipt of the Generale Keyserlycke Indische Compagnie, the Imperial East India Company chartered at Ostend, acknowledged by the shareholder C.J. De Witte at Antwerp on 11 August 1734 and signed by the company's cashier Joan Baptista Cogels. The form records payment of 360 guilders in bank money of exchange as a distribution of six percent, sixty guilders a share, on six shares held in the holder's name. The company had been chartered by Charles VI in 1722, and Britain, the Dutch Republic and France forced its suppression in 1731; this receipt belongs to the liquidation that followed.
goetzmann0412: A bearer bond of 1,000 Dutch guilders bearing 8 percent annual interest, dated Budapest, 1 August 1926, from the First Mortgage Loan of the Order of Norbertine Fathers, the Praemonstratensian Canons of Jászó, seated at Gödöllő near Budapest. Interest was payable by half-yearly coupons. The whole loan amounts to 1,600,000 guilders, divided into 1,200 bonds of 1,000 guilders and 800 of 500, secured as a first mortgage on the order's properties and guaranteed by the Royal Hungarian Government. It was administered by the Hollandsche Garantie & Trust Compagnie of Amsterdam.
goetzmann0413: An engraved certificate for one hundred shares of one hundred dollars each in the capital stock of the Oregon and Transcontinental Company, dated the twelfth day of September 1888 at New York and signed by Edward Ede as assistant secretary and by the president. The company's authorized capital of fifty million dollars is printed across the top of the sheet. It was the holding company Henry Villard assembled in 1881 to bind the Oregon Railway and Navigation Company, Pacific steamships and a controlling interest in the Northern Pacific into a single Northwestern transportation system; the structure broke in 1883. Engraved by the American Bank Note Company.
goetzmann0414: A premium debenture, the "Österreichisches Bau-Los, Em. 1926," of ten Austrian schillings face value, issued at Vienna in August 1926 by the Federal Housing and Settlement Fund. It forms one lot in a lottery loan authorized by the federal law of 27 July 1926: a total of 6,000,000 schillings divided into 600,000 such lots, guaranteed by the federal government and entered in the land register for housing purposes. Printed by "Steyermühl" of Vienna.
goetzmann0415: A provisional bearer certificate, dated at Paris, 26 June 1888, for one lottery bond of the Compagnie Universelle du Canal Interocéanique de Panama. The bond belongs to a 720-million-franc loan of two million lottery obligations authorized by the law of 8 June 1888 and offered without any guarantee of the State. Each obligation yields 15 francs yearly, paid half-yearly on 1 December and 1 June, and is redeemable either by lot or at 400 francs within ninety-nine years; this title is paid up to only 60 francs of the 360 subscribed. It carries the engraved signature of Ferdinand de Lesseps as president-director. The company collapsed in 1889, and stamps reading "REMBOURSÉ PAR LE SÉQUESTRE" record the receiver's later partial settlement of bondholders.
goetzmann0416: A founder's share issued by the Café de la Paix, a joint-stock company seated at 1, Allées Paul Riquet in Béziers, dated Béziers, 1 January 1921 and signed by two administrators. The company's statutes, deposited with Maître Vidal, notary at Béziers, on 11 December 1920, fixed its capital at 1,200,000 francs, fully paid, divided into 2,400 shares of 500 francs each. A founder's share carried no nominal value and was granted to a venture's promoters as a claim on profits above a set dividend. Lithographed by Cadenet Frères of Béziers.
goetzmann0417: A handwritten subscription certificate of the Republic of Peru, struck with the official seal, recording one share in the 100,000-peso emergency loan authorized by the Sovereign Congress at Lima in January 1823. The treasury promises to repay the holder, Santiago Campos, for his part of a 1,000-peso share, within one month of date, with interest at five percent monthly. The tally below sets principal at 66 pesos and interest at 3 pesos 2 reales 4, totalling 69 pesos 2 reales 4. The Congress declared principal and interest an irremissible national debt ranking before all other obligations, the money raised to meet public needs and to impel the army to end the war.
goetzmann0418: A blank stock certificate of the Philad'a & West Chester Turnpike Road Co. of Philadelphia, a turnpike chartered in 1803, with a par value of 25 dollars a share stated in the engraved left margin. No shareholder name, number of shares or date has been entered, and the printed line reads only "Philadelphia, the ___ day of ___ 18__": this is an unissued remainder. It joined the city to the borough of West Chester and was financed by subscription shares sold to local investors. Printed by Evans, Fourth & Library Streets, Philadelphia.
goetzmann0419: A fully paid bearer share of 500 francs in the Société des Plantations d'Agaves de l'Annam, a French colonial agricultural company seated at Saigon, dated Saigon, 31 December 1924. The text records an original capital of 2,750,000 francs in 5,500 shares of 500 francs each, with statutes deposited before a Saigon notary on 27 March 1924. Later overstamps record the company's financial history: a blue overprint raises the capital to 6,875,000 francs, and a red overprint reduces the face value to 100 francs by resolution of an extraordinary general meeting. The firm planted agave in central Annam, then under French rule, for sisal fibre destined for rope and cordage. Printed by A. Portail, Saigon.
goetzmann0420: A certificate for fifty shares of 1,000 Polish marks each, a block totalling 50,000 marks, in the Polsko Amerykańskie Towarzystwo Naftowe "Columbia," the Polish-American Petroleum Company, whose statute the sheet records as approved on 6 February 1922. It was issued at Warsaw and signed by the president of the council, the board, the bookkeeper and the treasurer. The company worked oil in the Galician fields of the newly reunified Polish state.
goetzmann0421: A bearer mortgage bond for 400 francs of the Compagnie Privilégiée des Ports, Débarcadère Maritime et Terrains de Cadix, dated Paris, 31 August 1869. The company was a French joint-stock concern constituted before the Paris notary Me Bourget, with its registered office at 15, Rue de la Chaussée d'Antin. Against a capital of ten million francs it raised a loan of twenty million, represented by 71,429 mortgage bonds issued at 280 francs and redeemable at 400 over twenty years. Annual interest of 24 francs was paid in quarterly six-franc coupons on 15 January, April, July and October. Printed by Paul Dupont, 41 rue Jean-Jacques-Rousseau, Paris.
goetzmann0422: A printed Certificate of Interest, lettered "B," attached to a £100 bond of the Three Per Cent Portuguese External Debt, confirmed by royal decree dated at the Palace of Cintra, 28 July 1856. The underlying bond was issued under the Portuguese royal decree of 18 December 1852. The certificate records the holder's entitlement to an additional one percent a year, granted under article 2 of the law of 26 July 1856 and deriving from an arrangement entered into in London on 13 December 1855. It was countersigned in London by José Jorge Loureiro, financial agent of the Portuguese Government, and its text appears in English with a parallel Spanish translation. Printed by Whiffing, London.
goetzmann0423: A prize-loan bond of the Royal Serbian Government for ten gold francs, issued at Belgrade and dated 3/15 June 1888 under the law of 20 April (2 May) 1888, which created a state tobacco monopoly. It is one unit of a ten-million-franc gold loan divided into one million such bonds, in ten thousand series of one hundred numbers each. The text runs in German, Serbian and French, and pledges the monopoly's revenues to the loan's interest, amortization and prize draws over sixty-five years, payable at Belgrade and Vienna.
goetzmann0424: A priority bond of 500 gulden, reckoned in the 24½-gulden standard and bearing four percent interest, issued at Wiesbaden on 1 July 1850 by the Verein zum Schutze deutscher Einwanderer in Texas, the Adelsverein or association of German nobles. The bearer holds a 500-gulden share of a 1,600,000-gulden total, ranking ahead of the ordinary shares upon the association's assets, under statutes of 16 October 1847 approved by the ducal Nassau government at Biebrich on 23 July. It is signed by the committee. The association had settled thousands of German emigrants in Texas, founding New Braunfels and Fredericksburg.
goetzmann0425: A printed promise of a territorial mandate for twenty-five francs, issued by the Trésorerie Nationale of the French Republic and created, as its text declares, by the law of 28 Ventôse Year 4, that is 18 March 1796. It bears the signatures of Bugarel and Chevallier and the notation "Vu au Contrôle." The note circulated as a stopgap before the full mandats territoriaux were printed. The mandats were meant to supplant the collapsing assignats, the land-backed paper drawn on confiscated national property; like the assignats they were nominally redeemable in national property, and like them they depreciated to near nothing within months.
goetzmann0426: A notarial deed of reconstitution of rentes, executed before the king's counsellors and notaries at the Châtelet de Paris and dated 20 July 1763. Printed on a partly engraved form and completed in manuscript, it re-establishes title to 3 percent perpetual and hereditary rentes created by the royal Edict of May 1760, registered in the Parlement on the 23rd of that month, which authorized 1,800,000 livres of such annuities. The income was secured on the duty on tanned leather established by an earlier Edict of August 1759, and on the king's other revenues.
goetzmann0427: A one-thousand-mark Reichsbanknote, a bearer note of the Reichsbank, the central bank of the German Empire, dated Berlin, 21 April 1910. The text promises that the Reichsbank's principal cashier in Berlin will pay the bearer without verification of identity. It was issued under the authority of the Reichsbankdirektorium, whose directors and deputies sign at the foot. It was among the largest denominations in ordinary circulation before 1914, when the mark was convertible into gold.
goetzmann0428: A one-thousand-mark Reichsbanknote, dated Berlin, 15 September 1922, issued by the Reichsbankdirektorium and payable to the bearer by the Reichsbank's main cashier in Berlin. A printed notice warns that from 1 January 1923 the note may be called in and exchanged for other legal tender, and a second clause threatens up to two years' imprisonment for counterfeiting or altering it. The note belongs to the early stage of the German monetary collapse of 1921 to 1923, when the Reichsbank was financing government deficits by printing currency.
goetzmann0429: A bearer bond of the République Chinoise for fifty United States gold dollars at five percent annual interest, dated London, 27 May 1925, and headed "Bon 5% Or 1925 / 5% Gold Bond 1925." Interest of $1.25 was payable half-yearly, the principal redeemable by annual drawings each December. Its text binds the bond to the Final Protocol of 7 September 1901 and the Chinese Indemnity, with service drawn from the revenues of the Chinese Maritime Customs and channelled through the Société Française de Gérance de la Banque Industrielle de Chine, the body managing that bank's affairs after its failure in 1921. The text is in parallel French and English. Printed by Vieillard, Paris.
goetzmann0430: A bearer treasury bond of 500 francs at 8 percent annual yield, issued at Brussels and dated 1 July 1921, one of 100,000 such bonds making up a 50,000,000-franc loan raised by the Government of the Chinese Republic to finance the Lung-Tsing-U-Hai Railway. It was placed through the Belgian-domiciled Compagnie Générale de Chemins de Fer et de Tramways en Chine, and bears the seals of the Chinese legation and a Chinese-character endorsement at lower right. The railway was an east-west trunk line planned across Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan and Jiangsu.
goetzmann0431: A bearer bond for 500 gold francs of the amortizable 4.5 percent Gold State Loan of the Kingdom of Bulgaria of 1909, issued at Sofia. The face value is stated as 500 gold francs, equal to 500 Bulgarian gold leva, and rendered in the leading gold-standard currencies of the day: 476 Austrian crowns, 405 Reichsmark, 19.163 pounds sterling, and 240 Dutch florins. The whole loan comprised 200,000 such bonds. Its text runs in parallel Bulgarian and French. Bulgaria had proclaimed full independence from the Ottoman Empire in 1908.
goetzmann0432: A share warrant to bearer of The Russian General Oil Corporation Limited, issued under the company's common seal in London and dated 1 October 1912, entitling its holder to one fully paid share of £1 sterling. The capital is stated as £2,500,000 in 2,500,000 shares of £1 each, and the text is set in English, French and Russian. The corporation was registered in England to hold and work petroleum properties in the Russian Empire. Later stamps record its voluntary liquidation in 1949, a winding-up order in 1952, and a return of capital to warrant-holders.
goetzmann0433: A bearer certificate, issued at St. Petersburg under an imperially confirmed resolution of 22 March 1902, registering an entry in the State Debt Book for the Imperial Russian Government's State 4 percent Rente, a perpetual government annuity. The face capital is one thousand rubles, yielding forty rubles of fixed annual income, and the certificate belongs to a series whose total value is ten million rubles. Its subtitle invokes the chain of imperial ukases and Finance Committee resolutions authorizing the loan, running back to an ukase of 8 April 1894. It was issued under the Commission for the Redemption of State Debts, and its final coupon is dated 1 December 1924.
goetzmann0434: A bearer share for 1,000 rubles in the Russian-Norwegian Timber Industry Joint-Stock Company, issued at Petrograd in 1917 to Jørgen Bjaaland, one part of a subscribed capital of 3,000,000 rubles. The charter was confirmed by imperial sanction on 29 December 1916. The text is set in parallel Russian and Norwegian. The company was organized to work the forests of the Russian north, where Norwegian capital had long traded in timber.
goetzmann0435: A bearer debenture for 10,000 kronen at 5 percent, dated Vienna, 1 March 1921, drawn on the larger loan of the federal capital city of Vienna of that year, issued at a total nominal sum of 1,000 million kronen and redeemable within sixty years. It bears the signatures of the mayor and the municipal council, among them the finance councillor Hugo Breitner. The krone was losing value rapidly at the time of issue.
goetzmann0436: A bearer bond for ten thousand marks in Reich currency, issued at Munich on 20 February 1923 jointly and severally by three Munich electricity utilities, Walchenseewerk A.G., Mittlere Isar A.G. and Bayernwerk A.G., as the Walchensee-Anleihe. Interest is not fixed but floating: the Reichsbank discount rate less two percent, capped at fifteen and floored at seven percent, with half-yearly coupons from 1 March 1923 and repayment at par beginning 1928. The loan funded the Walchensee hydroelectric works in the Bavarian Alps, underwritten by authorizations of the Bavarian Landtag. Printed by Gebr. Parcus A.-G. of Munich.
goetzmann0437: A bearer share of the Compañía Anónima de los Ferro-Carriles de Sevilla–Jerez–Cadiz, authorized by royal decree of the Queen of Spain dated 4 March 1857, representing one participation of 500 francs, stated equivalently as 1,900 reales vellón. The company's capital is given as 70,000,000 francs, or 266,000,000 reales vellón, and its duration is fixed at ninety-nine years. The text is issued in parallel Spanish and French, with coupons payable in Madrid and Paris. The line linked the sherry district of Jerez de la Frontera to the ports of Seville and Cádiz. Printed by Napoléon Chaix et Cie, Paris.
goetzmann0438: A Net Profit Sub-Certificate of the Shanghai-Nanking Railway, issued in London by the British & Chinese Corporation, Limited, under its common seal on the second day of December, 1904. It certifies that the holder is entitled, as one of not more than 32,500 such sub-certificates, to a share in the net profits of the line, the benefits secured by a Declaration of Trust of 10 July 1904 between the Corporation and the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation as trustee. goetzmann0496: A first bill of exchange drawn by the United States of America on 21 November 1778, ordering payment at thirty days' sight of sixty dollars, reckoned at five livres tournois to the dollar and thus three hundred livres tournois, to Jeremiah Green Esqr. or order, "for Interest due on Money borrowed by the United States." goetzmann0497: A partly printed, partly manuscript bill of exchange issued by the United States of America and dated the 24th day of November 1778. goetzmann0498: A printed and manuscript interest-bearing treasury note of the State of Massachusetts-Bay, dated the first day of January, 1780. goetzmann0499: An engraved bearer certificate for £500 sterling of Mexican Five Per Cent Deferred Stock, issued in London on 30 September 1837 under the hand of Don Agustín de Iturbide, Chargé d'Affaires for the Republic of Mexico, and countersigned by the agents for the conversion of the Mexican foreign debt. goetzmann0500: A printed and manuscript forward contract in shares of the Generale Keijserlijke Indische Compagnie, the Ostend Company, executed at Antwerp and dated in the printed close 10 November 1729. goetzmann0501: A New York State "Per Cent Stock" certificate, a funded public-debt obligation issued by the Comptroller's Office at Albany and dated 10 October 1815. goetzmann0502: A printed and manuscript notarial deed passed on 4 March 1817 before Everard Cornelis Bondt, public notary at Amsterdam, governing a negotiatie, a planters' mortgage-loan fund, of three hundred thousand guilders divided into shares of one thousand guilders each, of which two hundred ninety-four remain outstanding. goetzmann0504: A printed receipt, dated Amsterdam, 6 January 1894, recording the transfer of a single share, nominally 500 guilders, in the Dutch investment pool styled "Concordia Res Parvae Crescunt," through concord small things grow. Such pools gathered subscribers' guilders into mortgages and fixed-income paper.
goetzmann0505: A bill of exchange, the first of a set of four, drawn by the United States of America and dated the 14th day of October 1780. Payable at thirty days' sight to Jonathan D. Sergeant or order, it orders the payment of one hundred and twenty dollars in six hundred livres tournois, reckoned at five livres tournois per dollar, for interest due on money borrowed by the United States. goetzmann0506: A bilingual English and Spanish land-grant certificate, Class C, conveying 400 acres in "Poyais Proper," dated London, 28 April 1834, issued under the hand of Gregor MacGregor, styling himself "Cazique of Poyais," and countersigned at London by trustees appointed for the exchange and redemption of the outstanding Poyaisian securities. goetzmann0507: A printed weekly price current, the Prys-Courant der Effecten, issued at Amsterdam on Thursday, 16 May 1822 and numbered 39. The broadsheet tabulates quotations in two registers. goetzmann0508: An 8 percent bearer treasury bill for 1,000 guilders in Dutch currency, issued in 1923 by the Government of the Chinese Republic to fund the Lung-Tsing-U-Hai Railway. goetzmann0509: A handwritten plantation mortgage bond, No. 90, drawn on the Register of Middelburg in Zeeland and dated at Middelburg the first of January 1760. goetzmann0510: A French royal life annuity, a partly printed and partly manuscript receipt issued by Antoine Pâris, Conseiller du Roy and Garde du Trésor Royal, acknowledging receipt at Paris in 1723 of a principal of 1,175 livres in exchange for a yearly annuity of forty-seven livres, four percent of the principal. goetzmann0511: A partly printed, partly manuscript contract for a French royal life annuity on one head, dated 26 July 1759 and passed before the notaries and gardes-scel of His Majesty at the Châtelet de Paris and the Prévôt des marchands et échevins of the city, Jean-Baptiste-Élie Camus de Pontcarré. goetzmann0512: A £100 sterling bearer bond styled "Deferred," issued in London on 1 June 1845 by the Chargé d'Affaires of the Republic of New Granada under an agreement signed at Bogotá on 15 January 1845 between the Republic's Secretary of Finance, Juan Climaco Ordóñez, and Powles, Illingworth, Willson & Co., agents of the bondholders of the foreign debt of Colombia. goetzmann0513: A 4.5 percent Certificaat A for 1,200 Dutch guilders of the Rjasan Uralsk Spoorweg Maatschappij, the Ryazan-Ural Railway Company, issued at Amsterdam on 14 July 1903 by the Algemeene Trust Maatschappij. goetzmann0514: A Dutch administration certificate of 1897 for $1,000 of common stock in The Rock Island Company, issued through the Administratie-Kantoor van Amerikaansche Fondsen at Amsterdam, founded by the firms Broes en Gosman, Ten Have en van Essen, and Jarman en Zoonen. goetzmann0515: A lottery-loan share of 2.50 guilders, one of 400,000 making up a total loan of 1,000,000 guilders raised by the Vereeniging tot Bevordering van 's Lands Weerbaarheid, the Dutch association for promoting national defence readiness, issued at Rotterdam in May 1871. goetzmann0516: A printed certificate registering a claim to perpetual income yielding five percent, issued through the Imperial Russian State Commission for the Repayment of Debts and entered in the state debt book on 1 March 1822 at Pavlovsk. goetzmann0517: A French-language inscription in the Grand Livre de la dette publique de Russie, registered through the Commission Impériale d'amortissement and dated 1876. goetzmann0518: A printed certificate of the Imperial Russian State Commission for the Repayment of Debts, issued at St. Petersburg and dated 16 January 1839, registering a perpetual capital of 5,000 roubles inscribed in the holder's name in the state debt book under letter A, page 589. A perpetual claim on the Treasury rather than a dated loan, its French inscriptions refer to a rente perpétuelle entered in the dette publique.
goetzmann0519: A perpetual-debt certificate of the Imperial Russian Commission for the Repayment of Debts, issued at St. Petersburg and dated February 1854, recording a principal of 500 rubles in Russian silver coin yielding a fixed annual income of 30 rubles, that is six per hundred a year, paid in two half-yearly installments in January and July. goetzmann0520: A bilingual Dutch and French certificate for a 500-ruble inscription in the 6 percent Russian Funds in Silver, issued at Amsterdam on 19 May 1857 by the houses of Hope en Comp., Ketwich en Voombergh, and Weduwe W. goetzmann0522: A Dutch-language certificate issued at Hamburg on 13 March 1821, representing an inscription of five hundred roubles of 5 percent Russian funds, payable in metallic coin and entered in the great book of Russian inscriptions in the name of an administration established at Hamburg. Interest at 5 percent was collected for the holder's account against coupons under article 5 of the published notice, and the holder could at any time reclaim the original inscription against return of the certificate and unused coupons.
goetzmann0523: A bearer bond of the Volksstaat Hessen, the People's State of Hesse, issued at Darmstadt on 5 April 1923 by the Hessische Staatsschuldenverwaltung for the value of one unit of the state's 6 percent Braunkohle-Roggen-Anleihe, the Brown-Coal-Rye Loan of 1923. goetzmann0524: A bearer certificate headed "Conversion of Spanish Debt. goetzmann0525: A bilingual Dutch and French certificate documenting an inscription in the State Debt Book of the Imperial Russian Amortization Commission at St. Petersburg, issued at Amsterdam and dated 30 June 1825, entitling the bearer to a capital of 1,000 roubles in assignats at 6 percent interest. goetzmann0526: A printed certificate issued under the London Stock Exchange's Temporary Regulations for the Re-Opening of the Stock Exchange, applying Regulation 10 to a single bearer security: a City of Baku 5 percent 1910 bond for £20. goetzmann0527: A registered certificate of United States public stock, issued by the Treasury's Register's Office and dated 16 June 1792. goetzmann0528: A Dutch certificate of compliance with the law for the Uitgestelde Schuld, the deferred class of the national public debt, drawn for a capital of 1,400 guilders and issued at Amsterdam in March 1815. Gerlings signs as burgemeester.
goetzmann0529: A bill of exchange, partly printed and partly completed by hand, issued in the name of the United States of America and dated the ninth day of October 1778. Smith, Commissioner of the Continental Loan-Office for Pennsylvania, and signed by Francis Hopkinson, Treasurer of Loans.
goetzmann0530: A 5 percent bond of the Volksstaat Hessen, the People's State of Hesse, part of its Roggen-Anleihe or Rye Loan, issued at Darmstadt on 12 December 1923 by the Hessische Staatsschuldenverwaltung. goetzmann0531: A Continental Loan Office bill of exchange, partly printed and partly manuscript, dated 12 November 1778. goetzmann0532: A bill of exchange, partly engraved and partly completed by hand, drawn by the United States of America on the fourth day of November 1778 and numbered as the first of a set of four. goetzmann0533: A printed sheet of conditions governing a one-million-guilder loan of 1760, raised under the direction of the Amsterdam merchants Lever en de Bruine, with Samuel en Jacobus Walland as commissioners. goetzmann0534: A printed prospectus setting out the conditions of a lottery loan of 75,000 guilders, dated 9 May 1800, headed "Dankbaarheid en Erkentenis," gratitude and acknowledgement, and sanctioned by the Vertegenwoordigend Lichaam des Bataafschen Volks, the representative assembly of the Batavian Republic. goetzmann0535: A Dutch municipal charitable bond headed "Voor den Armen," for the poor, issued at Haarlem and signed the first of January 1805 by M. Bodisco, Receiver of the City Tax. goetzmann0536: A printed parchment bond of about 1647 to 1650, with its day and year completed by hand, a redeemable obligation of the Quarter of Zutphen within the province of Gelderland. goetzmann0537: A printed sovereign loan bond of King Gustavus III of Sweden, granted under the king's hand at Gripsholm Castle on 20 October 1784 and countersigned by J. Liljencrants. goetzmann0538: A printed Dutch-language obligation recording a sovereign loan of 1736 contracted in the name of Charles VI, elected Holy Roman Emperor, whose full Habsburg titulature opens the text. goetzmann0539: A bearer bond of the Internationale 5½%ige Anleihe des Deutschen Reichs 1930, the German Government International 5.5 Per Cent. Loan of 1930, dated Berlin, 15 August 1930. goetzmann0541: A printed copy of a notarial deed of obligation and mortgage of 1789, establishing a plantation loan fund secured on West Indian estates and placed with investors in the Dutch Republic. goetzmann0542: A bond certificate raising a loan in the name of the exiled French Bourbon princes, drawn at Amsterdam on 28 September 1793. Croese & Comp. acknowledges, on behalf of the Princes of France, receipt of one thousand guilders Dutch current for a share in the obligation, with coupons attached. goetzmann0543: A printed and completed forward sale contract in Dutch, done at Amsterdam on 13 May 1805 on a form supplied by the brokers Ricardo en De Lara, on the Weesperveld over het Werkhuis. goetzmann0544: A printed prospectus setting out the terms of a Dutch mortgage loan fund directed by Daniël Changuion, issued in 1816, raising 400,000 guilders for planters along the Rio Essequebo and Rio Demerary, in present-day Guyana, to continue and improve their estates, at 6 percent interest for a term of ten years.
